speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Is saṃsāra real, and what follows?
premises: Saṃsāra is not, in truth (tattvatas), for body-holders (tanubhṛtām).
Of bondage, what news (vārtā)? If bondage never truly is anyone's (bandho yasya na jātu), the liberation-rite (muktikriyā) is false (vitathā) for the free.
Diagnosis: an error-maker (mithyāmohakṛt), a heap of four delusions — rope, snake, shadow, ghost.
Rule: abandon nothing (mā kiṃcit tyaja), grasp nothing (mā gṛhāṇa); live (vihara) healthy (svasthaḥ), staying (yathāvasthitaḥ).
inference: Saṃsāra is delusion; bondage is unreal; the liberation-rite is false; abandon nothing, grasp nothing, stay.
uncertainties: Whether 'muktasya muktikriyā' means 'liberation-rite for the free' or 'rite of the liberated' is unresolved.
Whether 'vihara' is imperative or indicative is unresolved.
